subject: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, Apr 2, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Hi all — Support/CS needs a crisp “how to read the checklist” guide + macros before we roll beyond dogfood.

Asks (please reply inline by EOD Thu if possible):
1) Interpretation rules: when a step shows Not Started / In Progress / Complete / Blocked — what does it *mean* for troubleshooting?
2) Escalation matrix: which team owns which failure modes (auth, quotas/429, streaming disconnects, usage dashboard lag, eventing/state mismatch).
3) Admin override: what Support can do today (ENG-5852) and when we should escalate rather than overriding.
4) Known limitations we should preempt in macros (e.g., dashboard data freshness delay; out-of-order events; cohort flag).

Top tickets we’re trying to deflect with checklist + macros:
- SUP-18421 (401/403 invalid key/env var)
- SUP-18488 (streaming disconnect confusion)
- SUP-18510 (429 surprise right after launch)
- SUP-18544 (usage dashboard lag/mismatch)

I can draft macros, but I need the canonical wording + escalation owners so we don’t give conflicting advice.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Support Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Apr 2, 2025 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Jasmine — thank you. A few clarifications for Support:

Feature flag / cohorts (PM-768):
- The checklist is behind the ONBOARDING_CHECKLIST_V1 flag. During rollout, not every org will see it.
- If a customer says “I don’t see the checklist,” the expected answer may be “not enabled yet,” not a bug. Support should confirm org_id + whether they’re in cohort before escalating.

Step states (Console UX behavior):
- Not Started: we have not observed the event(s) required for that step.
- In Progress: we observed partial events (e.g., API key created but no successful request yet) OR the step requires multiple criteria.
- Complete: required criteria observed. It should not regress (ENG-5866 / race condition fix was to enforce monotonic transitions).
- Blocked: only used when we can detect a known failure condition (currently limited in MVP). We are NOT auto-diagnosing most errors.

Known limitation to message:
- Usage dashboard can lag. Checklist is not “real-time” for some steps due to ingestion delays.

I’ll let Dylan cover admin override + API mechanics.

Marissa
Dir PM, Console

+1. Please treat this as a go/no-go dependency for expanding the cohort.

Guidance for Support posture:
- The checklist is a *diagnostic hint*, not the source of truth. If checklist state conflicts with logs/usage/billing, we should trust gateway + metering data and file a data quality ticket.
- We should standardize “first questions” for each ticket type (key/env var, region, SDK/version, streaming mode, retry config, whether they’re using OpenAI-compat, etc.).
- For overrides: Support should use overrides only to unblock UI confusion (e.g., they did the step but it didn’t show up) and always annotate reason.

Jasmine — draft the macros and we’ll review quickly. Dylan/Marissa/Nikhil: please give her the specific wording and owner routing.

Alex Martinez

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 2, 2025 at 12:27 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Jasmine — details on admin tools + when to escalate.

Admin override (ENG-5852):
- Support can (a) mark a step complete, (b) reset a step, and (c) add a note. All actions are audited with actor + timestamp.
- Overrides do NOT emit onboarding events back into the pipeline. They only affect what Console displays.

When override is OK:
- Customer completed the action but step didn’t flip due to ingestion delay (e.g., created key, made first call) AND there’s evidence (screenshot, timestamped logs, usage row).
- Customer is blocked on an internal approval process but wants to proceed through other steps; we can mark informational steps complete to reduce confusion.

When NOT to override (escalate instead):
- Suspected out-of-order or missing events across multiple steps (potential regression; tie to ENG-5866).
- Any scenario where step completion implies security posture (e.g., “configured budgets/quotas”) and we can’t confirm.

Escalation routing (suggested):
- “Checklist UI missing / stuck loading / 5xx” -> Console oncall (my team)
- “Step state wrong vs reality” -> Telemetry/eventing owner (Logan’s team) unless clearly Console rendering bug
- “First 2xx never observed” but customer claims success -> gateway logs + metering (platform oncall) first; then telemetry

Known behaviors that look like bugs but aren’t:
- Up to ~5–15 min delay for some step updates (depends on ingestion). We are adding freshness indicators later, but for MVP: macro should set expectation.

If you want, I can paste the exact step criteria we’re using in MVP (what event flips which step) — but it may be easier to keep that internal and just guide Support on how to validate (logs/usage).

Dylan
Eng Lead, Console & Tooling
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Adding product-side framing + the “most common incident” playbooks.

How Support should interpret “First successful request”:
- This is derived from server-side 2xx response for a generation/chat request with a valid API key (not a console-only action).
- If customer insists they got a 2xx but the step is still Not Started, ask for:
  - request_id (or timestamp + region)
  - endpoint + model
  - whether they used OpenAI-compat
  - SDK name/version

Common incidents + what to say:
- 401/403: emphasize env var + key scope + which org/project they’re in (SUP-18421). Include “rotate key + re-test” guidance.
- 429: set expectation that default quotas exist; recommend backoff + check Quotas page + budgets (SUP-18510). Don’t promise immediate quota increases; route to Support manager for exceptions.
- Streaming disconnect: reassure that reconnect is expected on flaky networks; recommend client-side retry/reconnect patterns and timeouts; ask if they’re behind a corporate proxy (SUP-18488).
- Usage dashboard lag: explicitly state usage dashboard can be delayed and does not necessarily reflect real-time billing/limits (SUP-18544).

If you send a macro draft, I’ll edit for accuracy.

Nikhil
Dir PM, Hosted API

Subject: Re: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Thanks all — I drafted v0.3 macros + a one-pager cheat sheet. Please review wording around delays/overrides.

Attachments:
- OnboardingChecklist-SupportMacros-v0.3.docx
- ChecklistState-CheatSheet-v1.pdf
- EscalationMatrix-onboarding-checklist.png

Macro set included:
1) “Checklist not visible” (feature flag / cohort)
2) “401/403 during quickstart” (env var / org mismatch)
3) “429 surprise” (quota page + backoff guidance)
4) “Streaming disconnects” (reconnect, timeouts, request_id)
5) “Usage dashboard lag” (data freshness expectation)
6) “Checklist step seems stuck” (validation steps + when we can admin override)

Open questions where I need confirmation:
A) Data freshness language: I wrote “up to 15 minutes” — is that OK, or should we be more conservative?
B) Override language: I wrote “Support can mark steps complete in Console with an audit note” — any risk we should add (“doesn’t change actual quota/config”)?
C) Escalation owners: I pointed checklist-state mismatch to Telemetry, but we don’t have a named oncall in the macro. OK to keep it internal + route via #support-escalations?

If we can finalize by Fri, we’ll train Support on Monday before cohort expansion.

Jasmine

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Apr 3, 2025 at 11:02 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Support readiness: Onboarding checklist (Console) — macros, escalation paths, interpreting step state

Reviewed. Edits/suggestions:

A) Freshness: I’d say “typically within a few minutes; in some cases up to ~15 minutes.” That avoids a hard SLA.

B) Override: please add one sentence:
- “Overrides only affect checklist display; they don’t change your API configuration, quotas, or billing.”

C) Escalations: keep external macro generic. Internally, route via #support-escalations + tag Console if it’s UI/flag related.

Also: in the “Checklist not visible” macro, add a line asking for org_id + a screenshot of the left nav, so we can quickly distinguish “not in cohort” vs “UI not loading.”

Marissa

Looks good with Marissa’s tweaks.

Decision:
- Approved for Support rollout.
- Please add a short internal note: if a customer is blocked on 401/403, do NOT recommend “try another region/model” as a workaround — keep it tight to key/env and confirm org/project.

Next steps:
- Jasmine: publish macros + cheat sheet to the Support playbook page (Confluence: onboarding-escalation-and-triage-playbook) and announce in #support.
- Dylan: ensure Support has access to the admin override tool + confirm audit log visibility.
- Marissa/Nikhil: confirm the checklist copy in-product matches the macro language for delays + quotas.

Thanks everyone.

Alex
